text:
Marathon Petroleum shares rose 2.3% today as oil prices climbed to a 6-week high following escalating military tensions between Iran and the U.S. in the Middle East. Reports of Iranian attacks on U.S. Navy ships pushed crude oil toward $99 per barrel, and with U.S. refineries already running at 98% capacity, higher oil prices translate directly into stronger margins for refiners—the profit they make by turning crude into gasoline and diesel.

This move extends a sharp week-long rally; the stock is up nearly 10% since late August. Geopolitical risk premiums in oil prices, combined with tight refinery utilization rates and lean fuel inventories, create the conditions where refiner profits tend to expand—a dynamic that's been rewarding MPC shareholders as the conflict risks keep energy markets on edge.
